question: You're working on a school project and want to copy some text. Which keyboard shortcut should you use?
justification: Ctrl+C is the universal shortcut for copying selected text or files. Ctrl+V is for pasting, Ctrl+X is for cutting, and Ctrl+S is for saving.

question: Pressing Alt+Tab allows you to quickly switch between open windows on your computer.
justification: Alt+Tab is a quick window switching shortcut that shows all open windows and lets you jump between them without using the mouse.

question: To create a new folder quickly without right-clicking, you can press Ctrl+Shift+___.
justification: Ctrl+Shift+N is the shortcut to create a new folder in Windows File Explorer. The 'N' stands for 'New'.

question: In Command Prompt (CMD), which command would you use to see all the files and folders in your current location?
justification: The 'dir' command (short for directory) lists all files and folders in the current directory. 'cd' changes directories, 'mkdir' creates folders, and 'cls' clears the screen.

question: You're saving your science project. Which file name follows the best naming practices?
justification: Good file names are descriptive, use underscores instead of spaces, avoid special characters like '!', and include version numbers (V1). This makes files easy to find and organize.

question: Your friend has files named Essay_V1.docx, Essay_V2.docx, and Essay_V3.docx. What does this naming style help them do?
choices: Keep track of different versions and go back if needed
justification: Version control (V1, V2, V3) helps you keep track of changes over time. If something goes wrong in V3, you can go back to V2 or V1 without losing your earlier work.

question: The path C:\Users\Ahmed\Documents\Homework\Math_V1.docx tells us that the file Math_V1.docx is inside a folder called Homework, which is inside Documents.
justification: An absolute path shows the complete location of a file from the root drive. Reading from left to right: C: drive → Users → Ahmed → Documents → Homework → Math_V1.docx. Each backslash (\) separates folder levels.

question: You want to take a screenshot of your entire screen to show a friend your game stats. Which key captures everything on your screen?
justification: The Print Screen (PrtSc) key captures an image of your entire screen and copies it to the clipboard. You can then paste it into an image editor or document.

question: A .pdf file will look exactly the same on any computer, phone, or tablet, no matter what software is installed.
justification: PDF (Portable Document Format) preserves the exact formatting, fonts, and layout of a document regardless of what device or software opens it. That's why it's great for sharing final versions.

question: To capture only the active window (not the entire screen), you should press ___+PrtSc.
justification: Alt+PrtSc captures only the currently active window, which is useful when you want to screenshot just one application without showing everything else on your screen.

question: You need to find information about climate change, but only from educational websites. Which Google search would work best?
justification: The site: operator tells Google to only show results from specific website types. Using site:.edu limits results to educational institutions, which are typically more reliable sources.

question: You're researching space exploration for a school presentation. Which source would be the MOST credible?
choices: A website with lots of pop-up ads
justification: Government websites (.gov) and official organization sites are among the most credible sources because they're maintained by experts and verified before publishing. NASA is the official U.S. space agency.

question: Using the search "robotics project filetype:pdf" will show you only PDF documents about robotics projects in the search results.
justification: The filetype: operator filters search results to show only files with the specified extension. This is useful when you want downloadable documents like PDFs for research.

question: What is phishing?
choices: Fake emails or messages trying to steal your personal information
A type of computer virus that deletes files
A way to make your internet faster
A method to compress large files
justification: Phishing is a cyber attack where criminals send fake emails, messages, or create fake websites that look legitimate to trick you into giving away passwords, credit card numbers, or personal information.

question: A pop-up message saying "YOUR COMPUTER HAS 50 VIRUSES! CALL THIS NUMBER NOW!" is usually a scam and should be ignored.
justification: Legitimate antivirus software never uses scary pop-ups with phone numbers or urgent warnings. These are scam tactics to trick you into paying money or giving access to your computer. Close them without clicking anything.

question: You receive an email from "amaz0n-support@gmail.com" saying your account will be deleted unless you click a link and enter your password immediately. Which red flags suggest this is a phishing attempt?
choices: The email is written in English
The email was sent in the morning
The email contains the Amazon logo
Suspicious email address, creates urgency, and asks for password
justification: Multiple red flags: 1) The email uses a fake address with '0' instead of 'o' and @gmail.com instead of @amazon.com, 2) Creates false urgency ('immediately'), 3) Asks for sensitive information. Real companies never ask for passwords via email.

question: Your friend sends you a file called vacation_photo.png. What type of file is this?
justification: The .png extension stands for Portable Network Graphics, which is an image file format. It's commonly used for pictures, screenshots, and graphics that need transparent backgrounds.

question: Google Drive offers ___ GB of free cloud storage for every Google account.
justification: Google provides 15 GB of free cloud storage shared across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos. This is enough for many documents, photos, and school projects.

question: When working in Google Docs, you don't need to press Ctrl+S to save because it automatically saves your work as you type.
justification: Google Docs has an auto-save feature that continuously saves your document to the cloud as you work. You'll see 'Saving...' and then 'All changes saved in Drive' at the top of the page.

question: Computers understand information using binary. What is binary made of?
justification: Binary is a number system that uses only two digits: 0 and 1. Computers use binary because electronic circuits can easily represent two states: off (0) and on (1).

question: An algorithm is a ___-by-___ set of instructions to solve a problem.
justification: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure or set of rules to solve a problem or complete a task. It's like a recipe that tells you exactly what to do in order.

question: In the computer model "Input → Process → Output," what happens during the "Process" stage?
choices: The user types on the keyboard
The screen displays the final answer
The computer works with the data to produce a result
justification: In the IPO model: Input is when data enters (keyboard, mouse), Process is when the computer calculates or manipulates that data, and Output is when results are displayed (screen, speakers, printer).

question: In programming, if you write: IF score >= 50 THEN print "Pass" ELSE print "Fail" — and the score is 50, the program will print "Pass".
justification: The condition score >= 50 means 'score is greater than OR equal to 50.' Since 50 equals 50, the condition is true, so the program executes the IF branch and prints 'Pass'.

question: In programming, what is a variable?
choices: A container that stores data like numbers or text
A special kind of file extension
justification: A variable is like a labeled box in the computer's memory that holds data. For example, 'score = 100' creates a variable named 'score' that stores the number 100.

question: In a game, a player unlocks a bonus level only if they have MORE than 100 coins AND have completed level 5. If a player has 150 coins but only completed level 3, will they unlock the bonus?
choices: Yes, because they have enough coins
No, because they have too many coins
No, because both conditions must be true with AND
Yes, because one condition is true
justification: The AND operator requires ALL conditions to be true. The player has enough coins (TRUE), but hasn't completed level 5 (FALSE). TRUE AND FALSE = FALSE, so the bonus doesn't unlock.

question: The process of finding and fixing errors in a computer program is called ___.
justification: Debugging is the process of identifying and removing bugs (errors) from code. The term comes from early computing when an actual moth (bug) caused a computer malfunction!

question: Oops! You accidentally deleted an important paragraph in your essay. Which shortcut can undo your last action?
justification: Ctrl+Z is the universal 'undo' shortcut that reverses your last action. It works in most applications and can be pressed multiple times to undo several actions.

question: Pressing F2 while a file is selected allows you to quickly rename it without right-clicking.
justification: F2 is a quick shortcut for renaming files and folders in Windows. Simply select the item and press F2 to make the name editable.

question: In Command Prompt, you want to move from the Downloads folder to the Documents folder. Which command helps you change directories?
justification: The 'cd' command (change directory) is used to navigate between folders in Command Prompt. For example, 'cd Documents' would take you to the Documents folder.

question: In Command Prompt, the command ___ is used to create a new folder (make directory).
justification: The 'mkdir' command (make directory) creates a new folder. For example, 'mkdir Games' would create a folder called Games in your current location.

question: You're trying to save a file but getting an error. Which file name is causing the problem because it contains invalid characters?
justification: Windows doesn't allow these characters in file names: \ / : * ? " < > |. The file name 'Project:Final?.docx' contains both ':' and '?' which are invalid characters.

question: When working on an important project, it's a good idea to save new versions (like V1, V2, V3) instead of overwriting the same file.
justification: Saving different versions protects your work. If something goes wrong or you prefer an earlier version, you can easily go back. This is called version control.

question: You want to capture only a specific part of your screen for a tutorial you're making. Which Windows tool lets you select and capture a custom area?
justification: Snip & Sketch (or Snipping Tool) allows you to draw a selection around any part of your screen to capture just that area. You can also add annotations afterward.

question: You're creating a tutorial showing how to use a new app. Why should you add annotations (arrows, circles, text) to your screenshots?
choices: To make the file size larger
To highlight important areas and guide the viewer's attention
justification: Annotations like arrows, circles, and text help viewers understand exactly what to look at and what steps to follow. They make tutorials clearer and more professional.

question: Pressing Windows+___ takes a screenshot and automatically saves it to your Pictures folder.
justification: Windows+PrtSc captures the entire screen AND automatically saves it as a PNG file in your Pictures > Screenshots folder. The screen briefly dims to confirm the capture.

question: You want to find pages that contain the exact phrase "machine learning for beginners" - not just pages with those words scattered around. What should you use?
choices: Add exclamation marks: machine learning for beginners!!!
Separate words with commas: machine, learning, for, beginners
Use all capital letters: MACHINE LEARNING FOR BEGINNERS
Put quotes around the phrase: "machine learning for beginners"
justification: Putting quotes around a phrase tells Google to search for those exact words in that exact order. Without quotes, Google might show pages where the words appear separately.

question: In Google search results, the first few results labeled "Ad" or "Sponsored" are paid advertisements, not necessarily the best or most relevant information.
justification: Results marked 'Ad' or 'Sponsored' are paid placements. Companies pay to appear at the top. For research, it's better to look at organic (non-ad) results below them.

question: You found an interesting fact on a website you've never heard of. What's the BEST way to verify if the information is accurate?
choices: Check how many social media followers the website has
Cross-check by finding the same information on multiple credible sources
Only trust it if it has lots of pictures
Assume it's true if the website looks professional
justification: Cross-checking means verifying information by finding it on multiple reliable sources (like .edu, .gov, or well-known news sites). If several credible sources agree, the information is more likely accurate.

question: What is a computer virus?
choices: A harmful program that can damage your computer or steal your data
A useful tool that speeds up your computer
A way to connect to the internet faster
justification: A computer virus is malicious software (malware) designed to spread from computer to computer and cause harm, such as deleting files, stealing personal information, or slowing down your system.

question: A flashlight app asking for permission to access your contacts, camera, and location is a red flag that something might be wrong with the app.
justification: Apps should only request permissions they actually need. A flashlight only needs access to your camera flash, not your contacts or location. Excessive permission requests can indicate a malicious app trying to collect your data.

question: You want to download a popular game. Which is the SAFEST way to do it?
choices: Accept a file from a stranger online
Download from the official website or app store
Click on a pop-up ad offering free download
Download from a random website found on search
justification: Official websites and app stores (like Google Play, Microsoft Store, or Steam) verify that software is safe before listing it. Random websites and pop-up ads often distribute malware disguised as popular software.

question: After downloading software, you usually need to run the ___ file to install the program on your computer.
justification: Downloading copies a file to your computer, but it doesn't set up the program. The installer (usually .exe or .msi file) extracts files, creates shortcuts, and configures the software to work properly.

question: Your teacher asks you to submit your essay as a Word document. Which file extension should your file have?
justification: The .docx extension is the standard format for Microsoft Word documents. .mp3 is for audio, .png is for images, and .exe is for executable programs.

question: A .gif file can contain a short animation that plays automatically, like the moving images you see in memes.
justification: GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) supports animation by storing multiple frames that play in sequence. This makes GIFs popular for memes, reactions, and short looping animations.

question: Your friend sends you a .zip file containing their vacation photos. What do you need to do to see the photos inside?
justification: ZIP files are compressed archives that contain other files. To access the contents, you need to extract (unzip) them using Windows' built-in feature or programs like WinRAR or 7-Zip.

question: Your laptop suddenly stopped working, but all your school projects were saved on Google Drive. What happens to your files?
choices: Your files are only on the broken laptop
Your files are safe and accessible from any other device
Your files become encrypted and unreadable
justification: Cloud storage keeps your files on remote servers (the 'cloud'), not just on your device. Even if your computer breaks, you can access your files by logging into your account from any other device with internet.

question: Programming is the process of writing ___ that tell a computer what to do.
justification: Programming (or coding) involves writing step-by-step instructions in a language the computer can understand. These instructions tell the computer exactly what actions to perform.

question: Before writing actual code, programmers sometimes write "pseudocode." What is pseudocode?
choices: A plain language description of what the program should do
A secret code that hackers use
The final version of a program
justification: Pseudocode is a way to plan your program using plain English (or any language) before writing actual code. It helps you think through the logic without worrying about syntax.

question: In programming, if you want a character in a game to jump 10 times, using a loop is more efficient than writing the jump instruction 10 separate times.
justification: Loops allow you to repeat instructions without writing them multiple times. Instead of 10 lines of 'jump', you can write 'repeat 10 times: jump'. This makes code shorter, cleaner, and easier to modify.

question: In a game, the character moves right when you press the right arrow key. In programming terms, what is the key press called?
justification: An event is something that happens that the program can detect and respond to, like a key press, mouse click, or timer finishing. Events trigger specific actions in the code.

question: A game gives you a power-up if you collect 100 coins OR defeat the boss. You have 50 coins but just defeated the boss. Do you get the power-up?
choices: No, because you need both conditions
Yes, because OR only needs one condition to be true
No, because you don't have enough coins
Yes, but only if you collect 50 more coins
justification: The OR operator returns true if AT LEAST ONE condition is true. You don't have 100 coins (FALSE), but you did defeat the boss (TRUE). FALSE OR TRUE = TRUE, so you get the power-up!

question: You've just copied some text using Ctrl+C. Which shortcut do you use to paste it somewhere else?
justification: Ctrl+V is the universal shortcut for pasting content that you've previously copied or cut. Think of V as an arrow pointing down to where you're inserting the content.

question: Pressing Ctrl+A selects all the text or items in the current document or folder.
justification: Ctrl+A is the 'Select All' shortcut. It works in documents to select all text, in folders to select all files, and in many other applications to select everything at once.

question: What's the difference between Ctrl+C (copy) and Ctrl+X (cut)?
choices: Cut removes the original item when pasted; copy leaves the original in place
Copy removes the original; cut leaves the original
They do exactly the same thing
Cut is for text only; copy is for files only
justification: Copy (Ctrl+C) duplicates the item - the original stays and you create a copy. Cut (Ctrl+X) moves the item - after pasting, the original is removed from its location.

question: In Command Prompt, if your screen is full of previous commands and you want to clear it, you type the command ___.
justification: The 'cls' command (clear screen) removes all previous text from the Command Prompt window, giving you a clean screen to work with.

question: You're in the folder C:\Users\Sara\Documents\School and want to access C:\Users\Sara\Downloads. Which understanding is correct about navigating between these folders?
choices: You need to go up one level only
These folders are on different drives
You need to go up two levels (to Sara folder) then into Downloads
Downloads is inside the School folder
justification: From School, you go up to Documents (level 1), then up to Sara (level 2). From Sara, you can go down into Downloads. Both folders (Documents and Downloads) are siblings inside the Sara folder.

question: Using underscores (_) instead of spaces in file names is a good practice because some systems have trouble with spaces in file names.
justification: Spaces in file names can cause issues in web URLs, programming, and command-line operations. Using underscores (My_File.txt) or hyphens (My-File.txt) avoids these problems.

question: What does the Print Screen (PrtSc) key do when pressed?
choices: Takes a photo using your webcam
Prints the current page on paper
Captures an image of your entire screen to the clipboard
justification: Despite its name, Print Screen doesn't print anything. It captures your screen as an image and saves it to the clipboard. You can then paste (Ctrl+V) it into an image editor or document.

question: You're creating a tutorial and need to take screenshots. Which of these is a common mistake you should AVOID?
choices: Cropping the image to show only relevant content
Using annotations to highlight important areas
Capturing your entire desktop when you only need to show one small button
justification: Capturing too much (like the entire desktop) when you only need a small area distracts viewers and makes tutorials confusing. Always capture just what's needed and crop if necessary.

question: PDF is a good format for sharing final documents because the receiver can easily change and edit the content.
justification: Actually, the opposite is true! PDF is good for sharing BECAUSE it's difficult to edit. It preserves your formatting and prevents accidental changes. If you want the receiver to edit, send a .docx file instead.

question: You want to find articles about robotics, but ONLY from Wikipedia. Which search should you use?
justification: The site: operator limits results to a specific website. 'robotics site:wikipedia.org' tells Google to only show pages about robotics that are on Wikipedia.

question: To find web pages that have "Python tutorial" in their title, you would search: ___:"Python tutorial"
justification: The intitle: operator searches for words specifically in the page title (what appears in the browser tab). This helps find pages where your topic is the main focus.

question: While researching online, you notice that image searches for "CEO" mostly show men in suits. This is an example of:
choices: A stereotype being reinforced by search results
justification: Search results can reflect and reinforce stereotypes - oversimplified beliefs about groups of people. Being aware of this helps us think critically about the information we find online.

question: Which of these would be the STRONGEST password?
justification: Strong passwords have: uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, special characters (@!), and are at least 12 characters long. 'Tr0pic@lFish2024!' has all of these, making it very hard to guess.

question: If an email from your bank asks you to click a link and enter your password, you should always do it because banks need to verify your identity regularly.
justification: Banks and legitimate companies NEVER ask for passwords via email. This is a classic phishing technique. If you're unsure, go directly to the bank's website by typing the address yourself, or call them.

question: Which scenario is MOST LIKELY to be safe?
choices: Entering your password on a website with HTTP (not HTTPS)
Downloading software from the official Microsoft Store
Clicking a link in an email saying you won a free iPhone
Opening an attachment from an unknown sender
justification: Official app stores verify software for safety. The other options are all red flags: 'free prize' emails are scams, unknown attachments may contain malware, and HTTP sites don't encrypt your data.

question: To protect your computer from viruses, you should install ___ software.
justification: Antivirus software scans your computer for malicious programs (malware), blocks threats, and removes infections. Windows has built-in protection called Windows Defender.

question: You created a simple text file in Notepad. What extension will it have by default?
justification: Notepad saves files as plain text with the .txt extension by default. TXT files contain only text without formatting like fonts or colors.

question: You're saving a logo for your school project and need a transparent background. Which image format supports transparency?
justification: PNG (Portable Network Graphics) supports transparency, meaning parts of the image can be see-through. JPG doesn't support transparency - it fills transparent areas with a solid color (usually white).

question: Multiple people can edit the same Google Docs document at the same time, and everyone can see each other's changes in real-time.
justification: Google Docs supports real-time collaboration. Multiple users can type in the same document simultaneously, and you can see colored cursors showing where each person is working.

question: Why would you compress files into a ZIP or RAR archive before sending them to a friend?
choices: To add viruses to the files
To make the files impossible to open
To reduce file size and bundle multiple files into one
justification: Compression does two useful things: 1) Makes files smaller for faster uploading/downloading, and 2) Bundles multiple files into one archive, making it easier to share entire folders.

question: In binary, the only two digits used are ___ and ___.
justification: Binary (base-2) uses only two digits: 0 and 1. This matches how computers work with electrical signals that are either off (0) or on (1).

question: In programming, why does the ORDER of instructions matter?
choices: Because the computer executes instructions one after another from top to bottom
Because the computer can read minds
Because longer code always runs faster
justification: Computers follow instructions in sequence - the order you write them. If you put 'add sugar' before 'pour tea into cup,' you'd be adding sugar to an empty cup! Sequence matters in coding just like in recipes.

question: In programming, a function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task, which you can use multiple times without rewriting it.
justification: Functions are like mini-programs within your program. You define them once and can 'call' them whenever needed. For example, a 'jump' function in a game can be used every time the player presses the jump button.

question: In a game, a door opens when the player does NOT have a key (meaning keyFound = False). If keyFound is currently True, what does NOT keyFound equal?
justification: The NOT operator flips the value: NOT True = False, and NOT False = True. Since keyFound is True, NOT keyFound equals False. So the door would NOT open because the condition (NOT keyFound) is False.

question: A student wrote a game where collecting a coin should add 1 to the score. But when they test it, collecting a coin adds 2 to the score instead. What type of bug is this?
choices: A logic bug - the code runs but produces wrong results
A syntax error - the code won't run at all
justification: A logic bug (or logical error) means the program runs without crashing, but doesn't do what you intended. The code probably says 'score = score + 2' instead of 'score = score + 1'. Syntax errors prevent the program from running at all.

question: Pressing Ctrl+S is a quick way to save your work in most applications.
justification: Ctrl+S is the universal 'Save' shortcut that works in almost all programs including Word, Notepad, browsers, and image editors. It's one of the most important shortcuts to remember!

question: Pressing Windows+___ opens Task View, which shows all your open windows and virtual desktops.
justification: Windows+Tab opens Task View, giving you a visual overview of all open windows. Unlike Alt+Tab (which quickly switches), Task View lets you see everything at once and manage virtual desktops.

question: You have school files for Math, Science, and English. What's the BEST way to organize them?
choices: Keep files in the Downloads folder
Create separate folders for each subject inside a main 'School' folder
Put all files in one folder with random names
justification: A logical folder hierarchy (School → Math, Science, English) makes files easy to find. Keeping files on the desktop or in Downloads creates clutter and makes organization difficult.

question: If you name your files Essay_Final.docx, Essay_Final_v2.docx, Essay_Final_v2_REAL.docx, Essay_ACTUAL_Final.docx, you're following good version control practices.
justification: This is poor version control! Words like 'Final', 'REAL', and 'ACTUAL' are confusing. Good practice is using consistent numbering: Essay_V1.docx, Essay_V2.docx, Essay_V3.docx - simple and clear.

question: In Microsoft Word, you can save your document as a PDF by clicking File → Save As, then choosing ___ as the file type.
justification: Most document programs like Microsoft Word let you export or 'Save As' PDF directly. This converts your document into a format that looks the same on any device.

question: You need to send a screenshot to your teacher showing an error message, but your screen also shows personal browser tabs and a messy desktop. What should you do?
choices: Send the full screenshot including everything
Use Alt+PrtSc to capture only the window with the error, or crop the screenshot
Take a photo of the screen with your phone
justification: Professional screenshots should show only relevant content. Use Alt+PrtSc for single windows, Snip & Sketch to select specific areas, or crop afterward. This protects privacy and looks more professional.

question: You want to learn about "how volcanoes erupt" - what's the difference between searching with and without quotes?
choices: Quotes find the exact phrase; without quotes finds pages with those words anywhere
justification: Quotes tell Google to find that exact phrase in that exact order. Without quotes, Google finds pages containing those words separately, which might not match what you're looking for.

question: To find pages that have the word "tutorial" in their web address (URL), you would use the Google operator ___:tutorial
justification: The inurl: operator searches for keywords within the page's URL. For example, 'inurl:tutorial python' finds pages with 'tutorial' in the address that are also about Python.

question: A website ending in .gov is typically more trustworthy for factual information than a random blog because .gov sites are official government websites.
justification: Domain extensions indicate who controls the website. .gov is reserved for government entities, .edu for educational institutions. These organizations have standards for accuracy, unlike personal blogs which can publish anything.

question: You receive a text message saying "Your package couldn't be delivered. Click here to reschedule: bit.ly/3xY7z9" but you didn't order anything. What should you do?
choices: Reply to the message asking for details
Don't click - this is likely a phishing scam
Forward it to all your friends
Click the link to see what package it is
justification: This is a classic phishing scam. Red flags: unexpected message, shortened/suspicious link, urgency. If you're expecting a package, go directly to the delivery company's official website instead of clicking links.

question: A computer virus can spread from one computer to another through infected files shared via USB drives or email attachments.
justification: Viruses spread by attaching themselves to files or programs. When you share an infected file via USB, email, or downloads, the virus travels with it. This is why you should scan files from unknown sources.

question: You're installing a calculator app that requests permission to access your camera, microphone, contacts, and location. What should you do?
choices: Permissions don't matter, so just accept them all
Be suspicious and don't install it - a calculator doesn't need those permissions
Grant all permissions since you want to use the app
justification: A calculator only needs to do math - it has no legitimate reason for camera, microphone, contacts, or location access. Excessive permissions suggest the app might be collecting your personal data. Find a different app!

question: Fake pop-up warnings that say your computer is infected and you must call a phone number are called tech support ___.
justification: Tech support scams use fake pop-ups to scare you into calling scammers who pretend to be from Microsoft or Apple. They try to get money or remote access to your computer. Always close these pop-ups without clicking anything.

question: Your friend sent you a song file called summer_vibes.mp3. What type of file is this?
justification: The .mp3 extension indicates an audio file format commonly used for music and podcasts. MP3 files are compressed to be smaller while maintaining good sound quality.

question: Files stored on Google Drive can be accessed from your phone, tablet, school computer, or any device with internet access, as long as you log into your Google account.
justification: This is a key benefit of cloud storage - your files are stored on Google's servers, not just one device. Log in from anywhere with internet access, and your files are there waiting for you.

question: In Google Drive, if you want a classmate to see your document but NOT be able to edit it, you should share it with "___" permission.
justification: Google Drive has three sharing levels: Viewer (can only look), Commenter (can look and leave comments), and Editor (can make changes). Choose Viewer when you want to share without allowing edits.

question: When you press keys on your keyboard, what part of the computer model does this represent?
justification: Input is any data entering the computer - keyboard typing, mouse clicks, microphone audio, or camera images. The computer then processes this input and produces output (like text appearing on screen).

question: A recipe for baking a cake can be considered an algorithm because it's a step-by-step set of instructions to achieve a specific result.
justification: Algorithms are everywhere! A recipe, driving directions, or assembly instructions are all algorithms - ordered steps that, when followed, produce a predictable result. Programming algorithms work the same way.

question: In a game: IF player has a key THEN open the door, ELSE IF player has 100 coins THEN buy a key, ELSE display "Find coins or a key!". The player has 100 coins but no key. What happens?
choices: The message "Find coins or a key!" displays
justification: The computer checks conditions in order: First IF (has key?) - No. Then ELSE IF (has 100 coins?) - Yes! So it executes 'buy a key' and stops checking. The ELSE is only reached if ALL previous conditions are false.

question: In a game, to keep track of the player's score, you would create a ___ called 'score' and update it whenever they earn points.
justification: Variables store data that can change during program execution. A 'score' variable starts at 0 and increases as the player collects points. The value varies, hence the name 'variable'.

question: You want a game character to say "Hello!" 100 times. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Write say "Hello!" 100 separate times in your code
Use a loop: repeat 100 times { say "Hello!" }
It's impossible to make a character speak 100 times
justification: Loops let you repeat code without rewriting it. Instead of 100 lines saying the same thing, one loop does the job in 3 lines. This makes code shorter, cleaner, and much easier to change (want 200 times? Just change one number!).

question: In programming, an IF statement checks a condition that is either True or False - there's no "maybe" option.
justification: Computers work with Boolean logic - conditions are either True (yes, 1) or False (no, 0). There's no middle ground. This is why conditions must be clear: 'score > 100' is either true or false, never 'sort of'.

question: In a game, you want something special to happen when the score reaches exactly 50. Which condition correctly checks for this?
justification: To check if something equals a value, use = or == (depending on the programming language). > means greater than, < means less than. 'score + 50' adds numbers but doesn't compare them.

question: Professional programmers always write perfect code on their first try and never need to debug.
justification: Even the best programmers make mistakes and spend significant time debugging! Finding and fixing bugs is a normal, important part of programming. Testing your code and debugging skills are just as valuable as writing code.

question: To check if BOTH conditions must be true (like: player has key AND player is at the door), you use the ___ operator.
justification: AND requires ALL conditions to be true. If any one condition is false, the whole expression is false. Use AND when multiple things must happen together, like having a key AND being at the door to unlock it.
